charter_questions: Who are MetroGraph's direct, adjacent/foundational, and wedge-target competitors, and how do the ~158 registry companies cluster across the 11 archetypes (which are direct DB/graph-viz threats vs partnership/ICP-stack adjacencies)?
What is the canonical, frozen capability/feature taxonomy for DB & graph visualization tools, and how does every product score on support_level, quality_grade, and HCI cost (A-F) against it?

Where is the defensible whitespace — specifically, does any incumbent combine graph/DB-schema visualization + agent-workflow orchestration in a single low-surface-area (metro-map) view, or do they all specialize in graph-viz OR workflow OR schema OR notebooks?

How large is the market (TAM/SAM/SOM, CAGR) for DB-visualization aimed at noSQL/SQL startups + data engineers, and which segments score highest on attractiveness (WTP, accessibility, competition density, our_fit)?

Who is the ICP (segments + personas), what are their jobs/pains/gains, and which pains does MetroGraph's wedge (low surface area, best-of-both AI+UI, no agent-vs-graph-chat confusion) actually relieve and how strongly?
What is MetroGraph's value proposition versus each direct competitor (we_win_on / they_win_on / wedge_vs_them / their moat)?
How do competitors price (model types, tiers, free tiers, transparency), and where are the exploitable pricing gaps?
What is MetroGraph's Business Model Canvas, and which GTM channels and integration/partnership surfaces (Figma, Google Drive, the graph-DB engines, the modern data stack) should it build?

What does an exhaustive UX teardown reveal about the 'endless folders/panes/configs/popups' surface-area bloat (pane counts, click depths, time-to-value, drop-off risk, antipatterns) and the 'flee-to-AI-chat' / agent-vs-graph-chat confusion across the wedge-target categories?

What HCI, cognitive-science, graph-visualization, and RAG/agent-UX theory grounds the wedge — i.e., the evidence base for why reduced cognitive load, strong information scent, direct manipulation, metro-map metaphor, and copilot-first hybrid interaction win?

Which strategic, competitive, and demand claims survive adversarial verification (supported vs disputed vs refuted), with explicit theory grounding and recorded nuance, so the synthesis paper never over-flattens a contested verdict?

contracts.statement: The `companies` leaf is the sole first-writer of {{schema}}.companies and {{schema}}.funding_rounds and freezes every company.id (`market.company.<slug>`). All other leaves reference company.id read-only and MUST NOT insert company rows.

MetroGraph's own company + product rows use the reserved ids `market.company.us` / `market.product.us` with is_self=TRUE, written by `companies` and `value-prop` respectively; every us-vs-them query is a self-join on is_self.

The `market-landscape` leaf is the sole writer of {{schema}}.features and freezes the feature taxonomy (ids `market.feature.<slug>`, hierarchy, category, layer, kano_class) BEFORE any product_features are written. Competitor + teardown leaves reference feature.id read-only when scoring product_features (deterministic id `market.pf.<product-slug>.<feature-slug>`).

product.id is partitioned by archetype: each competitor leaf owns the products rows for exactly its assigned companies (`market.product.<slug>`) and is their only writer; no other leaf inserts products for those companies, so product PKs never collide across parallel writers.

{{schema}}.claims is partitioned per leaf by claim-id NAMESPACE (each leaf writes only ids under its declared prefix, e.g. `market.claim.comp.gdbv-native.*`) AND by the controlled category vocab it is allowed to emit. `market-synthesis` (paper) is READ-ONLY on claims and must never re-flatten or overwrite a verdict (conflation guard).

{{schema}}.reports is keyed by source_id (= sources.id); whichever leaf first ingests a source owns its report row (first-writer-wins on upsert). Every number in market-sizing/trends/pricing resolves to a reports or market_metrics row.

The `customer-segments` leaf is the sole writer of {{schema}}.segments and freezes segment.id (`market.segment.<slug>`); personas, jobs_pains_gains, pricing_tiers, and bmc_blocks reference segment.id read-only.

`customer-segments` owns the VPC customer-profile side (personas + jobs_pains_gains for the market ICP). `value-prop` owns the value-map side: it sets our_relief/relief_strength/addressed_by_feature_ids on existing jpg rows and writes the relief/differentiation relationships — the two leaves never write the same column of the same row.

The `pricing` leaf is the sole writer of {{schema}}.pricing_models and {{schema}}.pricing_tiers, referencing product.id/company.id read-only; it runs after all competitor leaves so every priced product exists.

The `partners-integrations` leaf is the sole writer of {{schema}}.partners and owns integrates_with/partners_with relationship edges; Figma and Google Drive are modeled as partners with relevant_to_us=TRUE even where the org also has a competitors row (coopetition).

Competitor leaves write {{schema}}.competitors as a ROLE overlay (company_id + product_id + we_win_on/they_win_on/wedge_vs_them) and the competes_with relationship; they never duplicate company facts (those live once in `companies` per C1).

Any ux_screen_ids referenced from product_features.ux_screen_ids must be created by the matching ux-teardown leaf (which is wave-ordered after the competitor leaf); teardown leaves own ux_screens/ux_flows/ux_patterns and link them back via feature_ids read-only.

Theory leaves are the sole writers of {{schema}}.theory_concepts (`market.theory.<slug>`); any claim.theory_concept_ids set by other leaves must resolve to an existing theory_concept, so theory leaves run in wave 1 before grounded claims are written.

Cross-entity edges in {{schema}}.relationships are written by their owning leaf only: competes_with (competitor leaves), partners_with/integrates_with (partners), acquired_by/invested_in (companies), grounded_in (theory + value-prop), substitute_for/belongs_to_segment (value-prop), synthesis edges (market-synthesis).

acceptance_tests: Coverage: every org in the master registry (~158) plus the MetroGraph self-row resolves to exactly one {{schema}}.companies row; COUNT(is_self)=1; no company appears in two competitor leaves' product sets.
Product-id partition (C4): zero product.id collisions; every {{schema}}.products row's company_id resolves to a companies.id; each competitor leaf's product count <= 10.

Feature-freeze ordering (C3): every product_features.feature_id and jpg.addressed_by_feature_ids and theory.applies_to_feature_ids resolves to a features.id written by market-landscape; no product_features row predates the frozen taxonomy.

Claims partition (C5): every claim.category is in the controlled vocab; every claim.id falls under its writing leaf's declared namespace prefix; no two leaves share a claim-id prefix; market-synthesis wrote zero claim rows.

Direct-competitor completeness: every is_direct_competitor company has a competitors row with non-empty we_win_on, they_win_on, wedge_vs_them, and >=1 product_features scorecard row with an hci_cost grade.

Teardown caps (C12): each ux-teardown leaf has <= 5 ux_flows; every ux_screen carries pane_count, click_depth and an hci_cost A-F grade; each teardown flags >=1 is_antipattern ux_pattern; any product_features.ux_screen_ids resolve to ux_screens written by the matching teardown.

Theory grounding (C13): every theory leaf produced theory_concepts with implication + strength populated; every claim.theory_concept_ids resolves; the six core cognitive/viz theories each ground >=1 strategic claim.
Reports first-writer-wins (C6): reports PK is unique on source_id; every numeric assertion in market-sizing, market-trends, and pricing resolves to a reports or market_metrics row with a source.
Segment-freeze (C7): customer-segments is the only writer of segments; every persona.segment_id, jpg.segment_id, pricing_tier.target_persona_id/segment link, and bmc linked_segment_ids resolves.

Whitespace claim exists: value-prop emits the headline supported/disputed claim that no incumbent combines graph/DB-schema viz + agent-workflow orchestration in a single low-surface-area view, grounded in >=1 theory concept and citing >=3 competitor leaves.
Synthesis integrity: market-synthesis writes only reports + synthesis relationships; every assertion in the paper cites a claim.id, and no claim verdict is re-flattened (conflation guard holds).
Acyclic waves: no leaf depends on a leaf in an equal-or-later wave; wave 1 has zero dependencies; the dependency graph is a DAG terminating at market-synthesis.
notes:
SCALE: blueprint scaffolds ~74 leaves (1 spine + 3 market + 24 competitive + 1 customers + 1 vpc + 1 business-model + 1 pricing + 1 partners + 29 theory + 11 ux + 1 synthesis). This exceeds the rough 25-35 hint because two forces dominate: (a) the 8-10-product competitor cap forced 24 competitor sub-leaves out of 11 archetypes (data-orchestration alone split 5 ways from 34 cos; internal-tools-lowcode 3 ways from 25); (b) the four parallel theory cartographers emitted ~39 'big_enough' subareas with heavy cross-area duplication, which I consolidated to 29 non-overlapping theory leaves (merged: mixed-initiative x2, cognitive-load+progressive-disclosure, DM-debate+prompt-vs-DM+copilot-vs-agent, Hick+Schwartz choice-cost, locus+autonomy user-agency, interactive-exploration+sensemaking, trust+RAG-UX+model-cards; dropped the 6 'big_enough=false' patterns into their parent leaves).

GRANULARITY CALLS: competitor leaves split on source/authority disjointness (engine-bundled vs DB-agnostic graph viz; visual vs dev ERD; rendering libs vs node-editors; iPaaS vs OSS; canvas vs conversational agents; BI vs notebooks; diagram-as-code vs whiteboard; ingestion/transform/orchestrate/engine/warehouse). Teardowns kept ONE per archetype (11) within the <=5-flow cap by picking the 5 most representative products. Theory and market-landscape carry NO company dependency so they sit in wave 1 per the brief.

DEPTH: defaulted exhaustive; downgraded genuinely thin/adjacent leaves to standard (foundational libs, graph-DB engines, BI, diagramming, most data-stack, peripheral theory) and scout (workflow-engines, warehouse-lakehouse). Direct rivals (graph-db-viz, db-schema-modeling), named wedge targets (workflow-automation, rag-agent-builders, internal-tools), customer/value/pricing/partners, the six core HCI+viz theories, and synthesis stay exhaustive.

SELF-JOIN READY: MetroGraph rows under market.company.us / market.product.us with is_self=TRUE (C2) make every differentiation/pricing/UX query a free us-vs-them split. pricing depends_on lists a representative subset of competitor leaves but reads product.id across ALL of them; wave 3 placement (after all wave-2 competitor leaves) is the authoritative ordering guarantee.

PARALLELISM: within each wave leaves are write-disjoint by the contracts (per-archetype product namespaces, per-leaf claim-id prefixes, single-owner tables for features/segments/pricing/partners/theory_concepts), so a wave can be fanned out to parallel writers with no PK collisions.
